clue.text: Follow four-wheeler to West End in two-wheeler

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a car is a vehicle with four wheels

indicators.note: End asks for the final letter of the word West standing beside it

explanation.surface: Someone on a bike or scooter trails a larger vehicle into London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' takes the last letter of West, so the West End, London's theatre district, is only a T here. The two-wheeler is horse-drawn, not a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light horse-drawn carriage with two wheels, once fitted with a box for sporting hounds.

clue.text: Buck's tenth original publication

parts.note: a buck is a US dollar, and a tenth of one is a ten-cent coin, a dime
novel as an adjective means new or original

explanation.surface: A man called Buck sees his tenth book come out in its first edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Buck is not an author but American slang for a dollar, so its tenth is the ten-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the American term for a cheap sensational paperback, the counterpart of the British penny dreadful.

clue.text: Dreadful girl one encountered on stage

definitions.text: Dreadful girl one encountered on stage

indicators.note: dreadful means in a bad state, so the letters beside it are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatregoer recalls a thoroughly nasty young woman met in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges GIRL ONE, and the whole clue also describes the answer: one of King Lear's two cruel daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the eldest daughter in King Lear, a wicked character who turns her father out, so an awful woman seen in the theatre.

clue.text: Mansfield, for example, houses art collection

indicators.note: a collection is an assembling of things, so the letters before it are gathered up afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stately home such as Mansfield Park holds a display of paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' is the anagram signal for HOUSES ART. Mansfield is not the Austen house but Katherine Mansfield, the New Zealand short-story writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Katherine Mansfield was a woman who wrote fiction, so she is an example of a female writer.

clue.text: Essay about love in the city of Paris

indicators.note: about says the word for essay goes round the letter for love

parts.note: to essay something is to attempt or try it
love is a score of nothing in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on romance in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps TRY round O. Paris is not the French capital but the Trojan prince of Greek legend who carried off Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris was a prince of this ancient town in Asia Minor, besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: A farm building liable to collapse

parts.note: a stable is a building on a farm where horses are kept

explanation.surface: A rickety barn looks ready to fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means not steady, switching between states, so something that describes is likely to give way.

clue.text: Extra crops cut, following calculations etc

parts.note: following as a preposition means after
maths is the school subject of calculations and the like

explanation.surface: Surplus harvests are reduced once someone has done the sums.
explanation.walkthrough: The original sense of the word is a second mowing of grass in the same season, which is what the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The literal meaning is second mowings of grass in one season, so additional harvests that are mown.

clue.text: Transparent dress material made of net — an eye-opener

parts.note: a toil is an old word for a net or snare, as in the toils of the law

indicators.note: opener asks for the letter that opens the word eye joined to it

explanation.surface: A see-through fabric made of mesh is quite a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' takes the first letter of eye; the hyphenated 'eye-opener' has to be split to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thin sheer linen or cotton fabric used by dressmakers.

clue.text: Female found in order to have a dance

definitions.meaning: a member of a lay sisterhood founded in the Low Countries in the twelfth century, a religious order of women
a West Indian ballroom step in bolero rhythm, as in the Cole Porter song

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a woman of a medieval lay sisterhood and a rhythmic West Indian ballroom step.

clue.text: One dropped from the air smashes into this

definitions.text: One dropped from the air smashes into this

indicators.note: smashes means breaks up, so the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged
dropped from says the letter for one is removed from the two words that follow

parts.note: one is written I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A parachutist or bomb falling from the sky hits the ground hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped from' removes I from THE AIR, leaving THEAR, which 'smashes' rearranges. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything falling out of the sky ends up hitting the ground, the planet's surface.

clue.text: Artist returning some time before noon

indicators.note: returning means the time of day is read backwards

parts.note: ten a.m. is one particular time in the morning, before noon

explanation.surface: A painter gets back home at some point in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TEN AM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard of that name was a French painter, a forerunner of the Impressionists.

clue.text: Sir Lucius put upstart in racing-boat

indicators.note: in says the single letter goes inside the knight's surname

parts.note: Sir Lucius O'Trigger is the fiery Irish baronet in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals
split as up start, the starting letter of up is U

explanation.surface: A knight seats a social climber in his rowing crew's craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside OTRIGGER. 'upstart' must be read as two words, up start, to give the first letter of up.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light racing shell with rowlocks projecting on brackets beyond the sides.

clue.text: New weapon contract

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament
an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A fresh agreement to supply arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract looks like the arms deal, but it is a verb here: to get smaller or tighter.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean to become tighter or less wide; a road can do either.

clue.text: Surface prepared for putting on one quiet colour

definitions.note: read loosely as a description of a tint, since the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: on tells you the first piece is added in front of the pieces that follow

parts.note: a green is the closely mown area of a golf course where the ball is putted
one is written I, the Roman numeral
sh is what you say to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: A base coat is made ready before a single muted shade is applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is golf's putting, not placing, and belongs with the surface; 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes a tint somewhat like that of grass, so it names a shade.

clue.text: Daily's written about one president

indicators.note: written about says the cleaner's name is set down around the single letter

parts.note: a daily is British usage for a domestic cleaner who comes in each day, a charwoman
one is written I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A newspaper has run a piece on a particular head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' puts CHARWOMAN round I. A daily is British for a cleaner who comes in each day, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is one who presides over a meeting, and this is a female who does so.

clue.text: European swings round sweetheart in French dance

indicators.note: swings round means the word for the European is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a Slav is a member of an eastern European people
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A continental man whirls his girlfriend about on a Parisian ballroom floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swings round' turns only the European backwards. 'sweetheart' hides a convention: read it as sweet's heart, the middle letter of that word, not a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the word in France for a waltz, used in English for concert waltzes.

clue.text: Cruel and hollow?

definitions.meaning: fancifully, having no core or centre, as a hollow thing has nothing in the middle

explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means without pity, and whimsically it means lacking a centre, as an empty shell does.

clue.text: Satirical act suddenly becoming popular

definitions.meaning: mimicking someone for comic effect, the act of an impressionist
what a product or craze is doing when its sales soar

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both mimicking someone mockingly and rapidly gaining success.

clue.text: Meaning to turn on spray

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the word for turn above the word for meaning

parts.note: to spin is to turn round
the drift of what someone says is its general meaning

explanation.surface: Someone intends to switch the garden sprinkler on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks SPIN above DRIFT in this down entry. 'Meaning' is a noun here, not intending.
explanation.definitionFit: It is foam blown off the crests of waves by the wind.

clue.text: His work secures a hearing for philosopher and economist

definitions.note: a description of a tradesman by what he does

indicators.note: a hearing for means the philosopher's name is taken as it is heard, not as spelt

parts.note: John Locke was the seventeenth-century English empiricist philosopher
Adam Smith was the Scottish economist who wrote The Wealth of Nations

explanation.surface: A man's writing wins two great thinkers an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hearing for' applies to the philosopher only: Locke sounds like LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesman fits and mends the devices that keep doors fastened, so his labour makes things safe.

clue.text: Two actors

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that says two is this while three is a crowd
a troupe of players who perform together

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb equates a pair with it, and a theatrical troupe is called one.

clue.text: Dull material military press may have to deal with

definitions.text: Dull material military press may have to deal with

parts.words: Dull material military press may have to deal with
parts.note: material is cloth and press is ironing, not journalism: the drab brownish cloth of army uniforms that soldiers must iron

explanation.surface: War correspondents are stuck with handling some boring copy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the drab yellowish-brown cloth of army uniforms, which soldiers must iron.

clue.text: Notice egghead occupying top position in college, say

indicators.note: occupying says the two short pieces sit inside the word for the top position

parts.note: the acme is the highest point of something
an ad is a notice in a paper
split as egg head, the head or first letter of egg is E

explanation.surface: People spot an intellectual holding the highest post at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' is the container signal. 'egghead' is not an intellectual: read it as egg's head, the first letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a literary word for the world of universities and learning, of which a school of higher education is an example.

clue.text: Male sabre-rattler holding a weapon

indicators.note: holding says the two words together have the single letter between them

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat
a hawk in politics is someone who favours aggressive, warlike policy

explanation.surface: A man making warlike threats is brandishing some arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal, and 'Male sabre-rattler' is two separate pieces, not one warlike man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the light war axe of Native American warriors.

clue.text: Letters set in faulty positions?

indicators.note: set in says the answer's letters are placed within the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Characters put in the wrong places on a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in' shows the answer sitting inside the last two words, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: They are printing mistakes, where characters have been keyed wrongly or out of place.

clue.text: Arrive in church to tie the knot

parts.note: to hit a place is to arrive in it, as in hit town

explanation.surface: A couple turn up at the chapel to get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is slang for marrying, and literally the verb means to fasten with a loop of rope.

clue.text: Ring may be present

definitions.meaning: where a piece of jewellery worn on a finger might be found

explanation.definitionFit: A finger band sits there literally, and the idiom means available nearby.

clue.text: City subdued league leaders in scoreless draw

indicators.note: in says the two initial letters go inside the pair of noughts

parts.note: a goalless draw in football is nil-nil, written 0-0

indicators.note: leaders asks for the leading letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Manchester City hold the top team in the division to nil-nil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letters of subdued and league, and 'in' puts them between the two noughts of a 0-0 result.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: The rest of the pupils perform on stage daily

parts.note: to play is to act a part in a theatre
The Times is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: While a few are absent, the remainder of the class act in a show every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' is a break, not the remainder, and 'daily' is this very newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: They are the school breaks when children stop lessons and relax.

clue.text: Daggers drawn when corruption is suspected

definitions.text: Daggers drawn when corruption is suspected

parts.words: Daggers drawn when corruption is suspected
parts.note: daggers are the printer's dagger marks, drawn in the margin by editors beside a passage of text thought to be corrupt or spurious

explanation.surface: Knives come out when someone is thought to be taking bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: They are the marks editors put beside passages of a manuscript believed spurious.

clue.text: Make a timely remark to stop me

definitions.text: Make a timely remark to stop me

parts.words: Make a timely remark to stop me
parts.note: what someone pouring a drink tells you, asking you to speak up at the moment the glass is full enough

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be interrupted at the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the pourer's invitation to call a halt once the glass holds enough.

clue.text: It's unconventional to use whip at start of race

indicators.note: at places the word for using the whip next to the word for the race's beginning

parts.note: the off is the moment a horse race begins
to beat is to strike, as with a whip

explanation.surface: A jockey breaks with custom by flogging the horse as soon as the gates open.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something unusual or eccentric.
